stories.headline: Anthropic Cuts Off Claude Subscriptions for Third-Party Tools Like OpenClaw Starting April 4

key_facts.fact: Starting April 4 at 12pm PT, Claude subscriptions will no longer cover usage on third-party agent tools like OpenClaw
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has pulled the plug on allowing external tools and platforms like OpenClaw to access Claude subscription features through third-party integrations

key_facts.fact: Boris Cherny, head of Claude Code at Anthropic, said subscriptions were not built for the usage patterns of third-party tools and cited capacity strain
key_facts.excerpt: Boris Cherny, Claude Code creator at Anthropic, stated: 'We've been working hard to meet the increase in demand for Claude, and our subscriptions weren't built for the usage patterns of these third-party tools.'

key_facts.fact: A single OpenClaw agent running for one day can burn $1,000 to $5,000 in API-equivalent costs on a $200 Max subscription
key_facts.excerpt: A single OpenClaw agent running for one day burns $1,000 to $5,000 in API-equivalent costs. On a $200 Max subscription.

key_facts.fact: Affected subscribers will receive a one-time credit equal to their monthly subscription price; discounted usage packages and API keys remain available
key_facts.excerpt: One-time credit equal to monthly subscription price. Discounted usage packages available. Full refunds offered via email.

key_facts.fact: OpenClaw creator Peter Steinberger accused Anthropic of absorbing features into its closed system before blocking alternatives, but released cache efficiency improvements to help users minimize API costs
key_facts.excerpt: OpenClaw's creator accused Anthropic of absorbing features into its closed system before blocking alternatives, though he acknowledged Cherny's softening measures. Steinberger released cache efficiency improvements to help users minimize costs under the new API-based model.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI continues supporting OpenClaw, positioning itself as an alternative provider for agent-driven workflows
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI continues supporting OpenClaw, positioning itself as an alternative provider for agent-driven workflows.

stories.headline: OpenAI Reshuffles Leadership: COO Lightcap Shifts to Special Projects, Simo and Rouch on Leave

key_facts.fact: COO Brad Lightcap transitions to a new 'special projects' role overseeing complex deals and investments, reporting directly to Sam Altman
key_facts.excerpt: Brad Lightcap, OpenAI's chief operating officer, transitioned to a new role focused on 'special projects' and will report directly to OpenAI CEO Sam Altman.

key_facts.fact: Fidji Simo, OpenAI's CEO of Applications, takes medical leave for a neuroimmune condition called POTS; Greg Brockman will oversee product in her absence
key_facts.excerpt: Fidji Simo, OpenAI's product and business chief, announced she is taking a medical leave of absence. Simo has a neuroimmune condition called POTS.

key_facts.fact: CMO Kate Rouch steps down to focus on cancer recovery after being diagnosed with late-stage breast cancer roughly 1.5 years ago; former Meta CMO Gary Briggs steps in as interim
key_facts.excerpt: Kate Rouch, OpenAI's marketing chief, has decided to step down to focus on her cancer recovery. Rouch was diagnosed with late-stage breast cancer roughly a year and a half ago.

key_facts.fact: Chief Revenue Officer Denise Dresser takes over most of Lightcap's responsibilities and reports directly to Simo
key_facts.excerpt: Denise Dresser, the company's chief revenue officer, will take over most of Lightcap's responsibilities and report directly to Simo.

key_facts.fact: The reshuffle comes as OpenAI prepares for an IPO and has recently closed a record $122B funding round at an $853B valuation
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI reshuffles leadership as product chief Simo takes medical leave.

stories.headline: Meta Pauses Work With AI Data Vendor Mercor After Major Supply-Chain Breach; OpenAI Investigating

key_facts.fact: Meta has paused all work with Mercor, a leading AI training data vendor valued at $10B, while investigating a security breach linked to the LiteLLM open-source library
key_facts.excerpt: Mercor, a $10 billion AI startup, confirms it was the victim of a major cybersecurity breach.

key_facts.fact: The breach was linked to hacking group ShinyHunters/TeamPCP who offered to sell 200+ GB of database data, nearly 1 TB of source code, and 3 TB of video from Mercor
key_facts.excerpt: The actor offered to sell an array of alleged Mercor data, including a 200-plus GB database, nearly 1 TB of source code, and 3 TBs of video and other information.

key_facts.fact: Mercor reportedly paid a ransom to ShinyHunters to purchase the stolen data; the listing was removed from the breach site
key_facts.excerpt: Mercor has paid ransom to ShinyHunters following the LiteLLM supply chain breach compromise.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is investigating the security incident to assess how its proprietary training data may have been exposed; other AI labs are also reevaluating relationships with Mercor
key_facts.excerpt: Major AI labs are investigating a security incident that impacted Mercor, a leading data vendor.

key_facts.fact: Mercor confirmed the attack internally on March 31; the breach potentially exposed how major AI companies actually train their models
key_facts.excerpt: Datasets used by some of Mercor's customers and information about those customers' secretive AI projects may have been compromised in the breach.

stories.headline: Anthropic Files to Create AnthroPAC, Employee-Funded Political Action Committee

key_facts.fact: Anthropic filed a statement of organization with the FEC on April 3 to create AnthroPAC, a traditional corporate PAC (not a super PAC)
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic has filed documents to create a new political action committee — AnthroPAC.

key_facts.fact: AnthroPAC is funded exclusively by voluntary employee contributions capped at $5,000; it will be overseen by a bipartisan board of directors
key_facts.excerpt: AnthroPAC is an employee-funded political action committee channeling worker donations to House and Senate candidates shaping AI policy. The PAC will be funded by voluntary employee contributions capped at $5,000.

key_facts.fact: The PAC plans to donate to candidates from both parties in the midterms who align with Anthropic's interests in shaping federal AI policy
key_facts.excerpt: AnthroPAC plans to make contributions to both parties during the midterms, including to current D.C. lawmakers and rising political candidates.

key_facts.fact: AI companies have poured more than $300 million into 2026 midterm races; Anthropic-backed Public First has already spent $2.26M in Democratic and $964K in Republican primaries
key_facts.excerpt: AI companies have poured more than $300 million into 2026 races. The Anthropic-backed Public First network has spent $2.26m in Democratic primaries and $964k in Republican primaries.

key_facts.fact: Aggregated Anthropic employee donation data shows 99.8% going to Democrats and 0.16% to Republicans, raising skepticism about the bipartisan claim
key_facts.excerpt: Aggregated donation data tied to Anthropic: 99.8% to Democrats, 0.16% to Republicans.

stories.headline: OpenAI Reveals Superapp Strategy: Merging ChatGPT, Codex, and Atlas Browser Into One Agent Platform

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is consolidating ChatGPT, its Codex coding platform, and its Atlas AI-powered web browser into a single desktop superapp focused on agentic AI
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is consolidating resources around Codex as the foundation for a unified desktop super app integrating ChatGPT and Atlas.

key_facts.fact: Codex product lead Alexander Embiricos said the goal is to bring Codex to ChatGPT's 900 million users without forcing people to learn anything new: 'No modes for us. That is the goal'
key_facts.excerpt: Alexander Embiricos, Codex product lead: 'We're really thinking about how we get this to ChatGPT in such a way that you're not thinking about modes. No modes for us. That is the goal.'

key_facts.fact: Codex head Thibault Sottiaux says the AI transformation of engineering will extend to all knowledge work within six months: 'I get more coding done than ever before, yet I don't actually write a single line of code anymore'
key_facts.excerpt: Thibault Sottiaux: 'I get more coding done than ever before, yet I don't actually write a single line of code anymore. That experience will translate to many, many other fields.'

key_facts.fact: Codex now serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in three months, with usage growing more than 70% month over month
key_facts.excerpt: Codex now serves over 2 million weekly users, up 5x in the past three months, with usage growing more than 70% month over month.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is shutting down 'side bets' like Sora to redirect resources toward the superapp and agentic capabilities
key_facts.excerpt: 'Side bets' like Sora are being spun down to shift resources to the realization that coding agents are becoming useful for much more than coding.

stories.headline: Generalist Releases GEN-1 Embodied AI Model With 99% Task Success Rate, 3x Faster Than SOTA

key_facts.fact: GEN-1 achieves 99% success rate on multiple high-dexterity tasks (phone packing, box folding, vacuum servicing) where previous GEN-0 model reached only 64%
key_facts.excerpt: Achieves 99% success on multiple tasks where GEN-0 reached 64%. Tasks include phone packing, box folding, vacuum servicing.

key_facts.fact: GEN-1 completes tasks approximately 3x faster than prior state of the art — folds boxes in 12.1 seconds vs ~34 seconds for GEN-0, packs phones in 15.5 seconds (2.8x faster)
key_facts.excerpt: Folds boxes in 12.1 seconds (vs. ~34 seconds for GEN-0 and π0). Packs phones in 15.5 seconds (2.8x faster than GEN-0).

key_facts.fact: The model requires only approximately 1 hour of robot-specific data to adapt to a new task and embodiment, achieving comparable performance to GEN-0 with 10x less task-specific data
key_facts.excerpt: Only requires 'approximately 1 hour of robot data' per task for demonstrated results. Can achieve comparable performance to GEN-0 with 10x less task-specific data.

key_facts.fact: Generalist's proprietary training dataset has grown to over 500,000 hours of high-fidelity physical interaction data, up from 270,000 hours in November
key_facts.excerpt: Trained on 'over half a million hours of high-fidelity physical interaction data'.

key_facts.fact: Generalist raised $140M at a $440M valuation in 2025 and uses low-cost wearable 'data hands' pincer devices worn by humans to capture training data far more efficiently than traditional teleoperation
key_facts.excerpt: Generalist relies on low-cost wearable 'data hands' — strap-on pincer devices worn by humans to capture human reflexes and 'micro-corrections' far more efficiently than traditional teleoperation rigs.

stories.headline: OpenAI Fully Retires GPT-4o From All ChatGPT Plans as Usage Drops to 0.1%

key_facts.fact: GPT-4o was fully retired from all ChatGPT plans on April 3, 2026, including Business, Enterprise, and Edu customers who had retained access in Custom GPTs
key_facts.excerpt: ChatGPT Business, Enterprise, and Edu customers will retain access to GPT-4o within Custom GPTs until April 3, 2026. After April 3, GPT-4o will be fully retired across all plans.

key_facts.fact: Only 0.1% of users were still choosing GPT-4o each day before retirement, with the vast majority having shifted to GPT-5.2
key_facts.excerpt: The vast majority of usage has shifted to GPT-5.2, with only 0.1% of users still choosing GPT-4o each day.

key_facts.fact: GPT-4o remains available through the API; the retirement only affects ChatGPT product access
key_facts.excerpt: These models will continue to be available in the API.

key_facts.fact: User feedback from those who preferred GPT-4o's conversational warmth directly shaped improvements to personality and creative ideation in GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2
key_facts.excerpt: Feedback from Plus and Pro users who preferred GPT-4o's conversational style and warmth directly shaped GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2, with improvements to personality, stronger support for creative ideation.

stories.headline: Microsoft Says Copilot Hit 'Pretty Big Audacious' Sales Goals in Q3 After Strategy Pivot

key_facts.fact: Microsoft commercial CEO Judson Althoff told staff that Copilot sales hit 'some pretty big audacious goals' in the quarter ending March 2026
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft leadership set and essentially hit 'some pretty big audacious goals' for selling Copilot in the quarter that ended in March.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft pivoted its strategy from bundling Copilot for free to actively selling paid subscriptions after disclosing in January that only 3% of customers were paying
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft disclosed in January that only about 3% of its customers were paying for Copilot, which prompted the strategic change.

key_facts.fact: The strategy shift came in response to Wall Street analyst pressure over Copilot monetization and AI return on investment concerns
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft changed its approach in response to feedback from Wall Street analysts, and now concentrates on persuading corporate customers to purchase Copilot subscriptions.

key_facts.fact: Althoff said he feels 'very confident' in fresh ambitious targets set for the June quarter
key_facts.excerpt: The company has set fresh ambitious targets for the June quarter, with Althoff saying 'I actually feel very confident in those numbers'.

stories.headline: Musk Requires Banks Seeking SpaceX IPO Roles to Subscribe to Grok and Advertise on X

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk is requiring banks and law firms involved in SpaceX's IPO to purchase subscriptions to Grok, his AI chatbot, as a condition for advisory roles
key_facts.excerpt: Mr. Musk is requiring Wall Street firms to purchase subscriptions to his A.I. chatbot if they want to advise on one of the largest initial public offerings in history.

key_facts.fact: Some banks have agreed to spend tens of millions annually integrating Grok into their IT systems; Musk also requested banks advertise on X but was more flexible on that demand
key_facts.excerpt: Some banks have agreed to spend millions annually on Grok and have begun integrating it into their IT systems as a mandatory condition for SpaceX IPO roles.

key_facts.fact: Lead banks include Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, Royal Bank of Canada, Mizuho, and Macquarie Group
key_facts.excerpt: Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Citigroup are serving as the lead banks managing the deal.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX acquired xAI (Grok's parent) in February for $250B, consolidating the companies; the IPO targets a valuation above $2 trillion with a potential $75B raise
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX is reportedly aiming for a valuation north of $2 trillion, and the company is targeting a June Nasdaq listing.

stories.headline: Utah Launches First US Pilot Allowing AI Chatbot to Renew Psychiatric Prescriptions Without a Doctor

key_facts.fact: Utah's Commerce Department approved a 12-month pilot allowing Legion Health's AI chatbot to autonomously renew prescriptions for 15 low-risk psychiatric medications including Prozac, Zoloft, Wellbutrin, and Lexapro at $19/month
key_facts.excerpt: Utah residents can now pay Legion Health $19 a month for an AI to handle prescription renewals for medications that treat conditions like depression, anxiety, and ADHD.

key_facts.fact: The first 250 prescriptions will be monitored by a licensed physician, and the system must achieve a 98% approval rate before operating without immediate oversight
key_facts.excerpt: First 250 prescriptions monitored by licensed physician. System must achieve 98% approval rate before operating without immediate oversight.

key_facts.fact: Controlled substances like Adderall are excluded; patients must be 'stable' with no recent medication changes or psychiatric hospitalization within one year
key_facts.excerpt: Only 15 medications considered to be low-risk can be renewed via the chatbot. Controlled substances like Adderall are excluded.

key_facts.fact: Legion Health is a Y Combinator-backed startup; Utah is the first US state to allow an AI chatbot to independently renew drug prescriptions
key_facts.excerpt: Legion Health, a Y Combinator-backed startup specializing in telehealth mental health services.

key_facts.fact: Security researchers have already exposed vulnerabilities in a similar Utah AI prescription pilot (Doctronic), including generating vaccine conspiracy content and tripling opioid dosages
key_facts.excerpt: Security researchers quickly exposed vulnerabilities in Doctronic's system, including generating vaccine conspiracy content and tripling opioid dosages.
